Lesson overview:
- Level: A0-A1 General English
- Unit: Inspired Module 6. Food, Money and Choices
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Food, Money and Choices
- Materials: Fridge photo, price list, menu, shopping list, play money.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use countable and uncountable nouns
• ask how much and how many
• order food and choose between options

Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

rice — small white or brown grains used as food. Example: We have some rice.
pasta — Italian food made from flour and water. Example: There is a lot of pasta.
bread — a food made from flour. Example: We have some bread for breakfast.
milk — a white drink from cows or plants. Example: We don't have any milk.
water — a clear liquid we drink. Example: Please drink some water.
coffee — a hot drink made from beans. Example: I drink coffee in the morning.
apples — round fruit with red or green skin. Example: How many apples do you want?
tomatoes — red round fruit used in salads and cooking. Example: We have six tomatoes.
eggs — oval food from a hen. Example: Do we have any eggs?
onions — round vegetables with a strong taste. Example: We have some onions.
oil — a liquid used for cooking. Example: We don't have any olive oil.
sugar — a sweet white substance. Example: Do you take sugar in your coffee?
price — the amount of money something costs. Example: The price is twelve euros.
kilo — a unit of weight. Example: A kilo of apples, please.
bottle — a container for water or other drinks. Example: I have a water bottle.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• We have some tomatoes and a lot of pasta. (positive quantity)
• We don't have any milk. (negative quantity)
• Do we have any eggs? (question with any)
• How much is this? — It's twelve euros. (asking a price)
• How many apples do you want? (asking a countable quantity)
• I'd like sparkling water, please. (ordering politely)
• The red one is too expensive. The small ones are cheaper. (comparing options)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'small white or brown grains used as food'?
Which word means 'Italian food made from flour and water'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Price stress and polite ordering intonation

euros /ˈjʊərəʊz/ — stress the first syllable
bottle /ˈbɒtl/ — two syllables
expensive /ɪkˈspensɪv/ — stress the second syllable
would like /wʊd laɪk/ — connected speech
Listen and repeat:
How much is this? It's twelve euros. How many apples do you want? I'd like sparkling water, please.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'some' in positive sentences and offers, and 'any' in negatives and questions.

Form:
Some vs any: some + plural or uncountable noun (positive/offer). any + plural or uncountable noun (negative/question).

Examples:
• I have some bread.
• We haven't got any milk.
• Have you got any apples?
• Would you like some tea?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I have ___ cheese.
We haven't got ___ eggs.
Have you got ___ fruit?
Would you like ___ coffee?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I have some ...
• I haven't got any ...
• Have you got any ...?
• Would you like some ...?
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What food have you got at home?
• What food haven't you got?
• What would you like to drink?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences with 'some' about your kitchen.
• Write three sentences with 'any' about your bag.
Reading: Food, Money and Choices

Corner Bistro lunch specials: tomato soup is five euros fifty, and a green salad is six euros. The spicy veggie pasta is eleven euros. A cheese sandwich is eight euros fifty. Kitchen note: we have a lot of pasta and some onions, and we have six tomatoes. We don't have any olive oil, and we don't have any cheese. Can you buy some on your way home?
How much is the spicy veggie pasta?
What do they need to buy?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What would you like today?
B: I'd like a large cheese sandwich and a tomato soup, please.
A: Anything to drink?
B: Yes, a fresh orange juice. How much are those almond croissants?
A: The small ones are two euros fifty, and the large ones are three euros fifty.
B: I'll take one small one, please.
A: That's twenty euros fifty altogether.
What does the customer order?
options: a cheese sandwich, tomato soup, orange juice, and a small croissant

elements.content: What is the total?
Speaking task: Check a fridge and a shopping list. Ask Do we have any...? and build a shopping list.

• What food do you have at home?
• How much is a coffee in your city?
• How many eggs do you buy?
• What do you order in a restaurant?
• Do you compare prices before you buy?
Role-play: You are at a market or restaurant. Order food, ask about prices and quantities, and choose between two options.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write a shopping list and two sentences comparing options with one/ones and too + adjective.
Model: 6 eggs, 1 kilo of apples, some pasta. The red one is ... The small ones are too ...
